what: The code holds no comments: about 1,110 were removed from the Python and 175 lines from the pages' scripts and styles. Docstrings stay.
The automated checks now fail on any new comment, naming the file and line and saying to use a name or a test instead.
Three comments are kept on purpose, each with its reason, in a list capped at 10 (docs/agents/local/comments-kept.json).
A push from this clone is refused in about half a second when it carries a comment; the settings stop an agent skipping that.
The browser tests run about a quarter faster, and the settings refuse the building agent Docker.
so_what: The next agent that reads this code no longer sees comments to copy, and the checks stop it if it writes one.
You can read the kept list to see exactly which comments remain and why; a change to it is named on the pull request.
Try it first: add a comment to any Python file and run python3 checks.py patterns; it goes red with the file and line.
A full run of the automated checks took about 2 minutes at the end of this build, against about 3 at its start.
now_what: One issue was left for you: display.py still holds three date and column-width settings no page uses. The spec lists such code; it does not change it.
Count before and after: the Python held 1,111 comments in 82 files, the scripts and styles 175 lines in 20 files; both are now 0, plus 3 kept.
Proof that only comments went: the 82 changed Python files have the same syntax tree as before; in the scripts and styles 129 lines went, 46 were cut and none changed otherwise.
Four facts that only a comment held are now tests: a registry code with a bracket is refused, and three more in monitor.py and storage.py (issues 01 to 04 of the review).
Kept comment 1, dialog.js: the opener may be redrawn while its dialog is open, so focus is sought by id. No test can see it.
Kept comment 2, dialog.js: focus goes back after the browser's own restore, which would otherwise win. No test fails without the delay.
Kept comment 3, focus.js: a disabled control loses focus a moment after a change, the reason for the 60 ms check. No test fails without it.
The push hook is switched on in this clone only; another clone runs git config core.hooksPath .githooks once, and the checks remind it.
The builder timed the hook in a copy of the repo: a push with a comment was refused in 0.42 s, and a clean push went through in 1.15 s.
The settings file was edited directly, so no settings-edit.md was needed. It now refuses a push with --no-verify, docker, docker-compose and opening Docker.
The Docker refusal also stops the agent opening any file with docker in its path. That is broader than asked; narrow it if it gets in the way.
Browser tests, one full run: 157 s before the stand-in registry fix, 127 s after; 124 s before the broken-pages fix, 109 s after.
The broken pages now run once per run of the browser tests instead of four times.
To save that time the guard tests now run first; every other browser test keeps its order. Without the reordering they still run once, but nothing is saved.
Defaults used as the spec named them, unconfirmed by you: docstrings stay, non-code files keep comments, the list caps at 10, no exploratory testing, Docker refused.
No exploratory testing was done: the spec rules it out because the pages changed in comments only, and one code review read the whole change.
Every changed browser test (86, almost all for removed comments) is left out of the walk-through except the whole-app keyboard walk, which shows the app works as before.
Linux was not checked here; the checks run on GitHub when the pull request is opened are where it is checked.

walk_through.title: The whole app works as before, now that its comments are gone
walk_through.legend: By keyboard alone: a watchlist is made, trials are added, a saved search finds new ones, a change is reviewed and dismissed, the summary is copied and the list exported. Each step should end as it did before.
